12-octopus-hearts.name: Octopus Three Hearts
12-octopus-hearts.idea: An octopus has three hearts and blue, copper-based blood that carries less oxygen, so it needs extra pumps.
12-octopus-hearts.title: Why an octopus has THREE hearts (and blue blood)
12-octopus-hearts.hook: Three hearts. Blue blood. One octopus.
12-octopus-hearts.body: Two small hearts push blood through the gills and a bigger one sends it round the body. Octopus blood uses copper instead of iron, which turns it blue, but it carries less oxygen, so it needs the extra pumping.

13-blue-sky.name: Why The Sky Is Blue
13-blue-sky.idea: Air molecules scatter short blue waves much more than red ones, so blue reaches us from every direction; at sunset the blue is scattered away.
13-blue-sky.title: Sunlight is white… so why is the sky BLUE?
13-blue-sky.hook: Sunlight is white. So where does all that blue come from?
13-blue-sky.body: Tiny gas molecules in the air bounce short blue light waves around far more than long red ones, so blue reaches your eyes from every part of the sky. At sunset the light crosses much more air, the blue is scattered away and the reds are left.

14-honey.name: Honey Never Spoils
14-honey.idea: Honey is so dry, acidic and full of a bee enzyme that makes hydrogen peroxide that germs can't survive in it.
14-honey.title: Why honey basically NEVER goes bad
14-honey.hook: Most food rots in days. Honey can last for years.
14-honey.body: Honey has so little water that germs landing in it dry out and die. It's also acidic, and bees add an enzyme that slowly makes hydrogen peroxide, a natural germ killer. Keep the jar sealed so it can't soak up water.

15-eiffel-tower.name: Eiffel Tower Grows
15-eiffel-tower.idea: The Eiffel Tower's iron expands in summer heat, so it can stand up to 15 cm taller, then shrinks in winter.
15-eiffel-tower.title: The Eiffel Tower GROWS every summer 🔥
15-eiffel-tower.hook: The Eiffel Tower is taller in summer than in winter.
15-eiffel-tower.body: Iron grows a tiny bit when it heats up. Each metre only stretches a fraction of a millimetre, but over 300 metres it adds up: on the hottest days the tower can be up to 15 cm taller. In winter it shrinks back.

16-banana-berry.name: Banana Is A Berry
16-banana-berry.idea: Botanically, bananas are berries but strawberries are not; a strawberry's dots are its real fruits.
16-banana-berry.title: A banana is a berry. A strawberry is NOT 🍌🍓
16-banana-berry.hook: A banana is a berry. A strawberry isn't.
16-banana-berry.body: To a botanist, a true berry grows from one flower with one ovary and keeps its seeds inside the flesh: bananas, grapes, tomatoes, even watermelons. A strawberry grows from a flower with many ovaries, and the dots on the outside are tiny fruits, each holding a seed.

17-onion-tears.name: Why Onions Make You Cry
17-onion-tears.idea: Cutting an onion mixes sulfur chemicals with an enzyme, making an irritating gas that triggers tears.
17-onion-tears.title: Why onions make you CRY (and the trick to stop it)
17-onion-tears.hook: Why does chopping an onion make you cry?
17-onion-tears.body: An onion keeps sulfur chemicals and an enzyme apart. Your knife breaks the cells, they mix and make an irritating gas that floats up to your eyes. Nerves feel the sting and your tear glands flood them. Tip: chill the onion first and less gas escapes.

18-dead-sea.name: Floating In The Dead Sea
18-dead-sea.idea: The Dead Sea is almost ten times saltier than the ocean, so its water is denser than your body and pushes you up.
18-dead-sea.title: Why you CAN'T sink in the Dead Sea
18-dead-sea.hook: In the Dead Sea you float without even trying.
18-dead-sea.body: It's almost ten times saltier than the ocean, so the water is much heavier than your body. When you get in, you push aside water that weighs more than you do, and it shoves you back up. You bob like a cork. Just keep it out of your eyes.

19-lightning-sun.name: Lightning Hotter Than Sun
19-lightning-sun.idea: Lightning heats air to about 30,000°C, five times hotter than the Sun's surface, and the blast of air makes thunder.
19-lightning-sun.title: Lightning is HOTTER than the Sun ⚡
19-lightning-sun.hook: One bolt of lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
19-lightning-sun.body: The Sun's surface is about 5,500°C. Lightning heats the air around it to about 30,000°C in a split second. That air blasts outward so fast it makes a shock wave, and that boom is thunder.

20-recorded-voice.name: Your Recorded Voice
20-recorded-voice.idea: You hear your own voice through air and through skull bones, which boost low notes; a recording only catches the air part.
20-recorded-voice.title: Why your voice sounds WEIRD on recordings
20-recorded-voice.hook: Why does your voice sound so weird on a recording?
20-recorded-voice.body: When you talk you hear yourself two ways: through the air to your ears, and through the bones of your skull. Bones carry low notes well, so you sound deeper inside your head. A microphone only hears the air part, and that's how everyone else hears you.

21-great-wall.name: Great Wall From Space
21-great-wall.idea: Astronauts say the Great Wall isn't really visible from orbit: it's only road-width and the same colour as the land.
21-great-wall.title: Can you see the Great Wall from space? Astronauts say NO
21-great-wall.hook: You've heard you can see the Great Wall from space. Not really.
21-great-wall.body: The wall is incredibly long but in most places only a few metres wide, about as wide as a road. From orbit, hundreds of kilometres up, that's far too thin, and it's built from stone and earth the same colour as the land around it.
